concept: Slot is the narrow mouth a room or a device unit has for a scene card. It is a recessed slit in the plastic with the room's name printed under it and a lamp beside it. Inserting a SceneCard runs the scene, the card then stands half out of the slit with its name readable, and the lamp lights with a word.

default_to_avoid.pattern: drop zone slot drawn as a dashed rounded rectangle that says drop here and highlights in the brand colour
default_to_avoid.why_not: P4 makes every hole a recess with inverse light, so the slot is a slit cut into the plastic, and P1 keeps orange off everything but the unit's one loud part.

default_to_avoid.pattern: slot that only accepts a dragged card
default_to_avoid.why_not: P3 asks for a keyboard map for every mechanism, so a held card goes in with Enter or a press on the slot, and dragging is the shortcut.

references.source: Yoto Player: the card slot on the top of the unit, the card standing half out while it plays
Braun cassette and card slots on Ulm school appliances: a slit in the case with its function printed beside it
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, keyboard drag and drop guidance: pick up, move, drop and cancel, each announced

derivation.consequence: each hole is a recess (inverse light), never a printed dot
derivation.form: The slot is a slit cut into the plastic with the well's inverse light, so it reads as a hole a card can go into.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The bay above the slit keeps a half card's height when empty, so inserting a card never moves the rest of the unit.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The room's name and the lamp with its word are printed on one line under the slit, and the empty bay prints where the card goes.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: Neither the slot nor the card in it is orange; a running scene is told by Badge's lamp and the word Running.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map (arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press) and a visible value and label
derivation.form: Arrows walk between slots, Enter inserts the held card or takes the inserted one out, and a polite status says Movie night inserted into Living room.

derivation.consequence: fast in, slow out, through the state motion tokens
derivation.form: An inserted card slides down into the slit once on the release timing and stays still; under reduce motion it is there at once.

options.name: top-loading slit: the card stands half out above a slit, name readable, lamp and room printed under it
side reader: a mouth on the unit's side, the card sticking out past the end
dock bed: a recessed bed the whole card lies in

variants.reason: A keeps a fixed bay so nothing reflows (P6) and shows the name on the edge that stays out, with the slit a true recess (P4); B cuts the name and widens the unit on a phone, and C is a drop zone, not a slot the card goes into.

root.why: The slot takes a card's width and a fixed height, so it sits in a unit beside the knob without moving it.

mouth.why: The bay and the slit together are one button well over 44px, so a press anywhere on the slot inserts or takes out.

bay.why: The bay above the slit keeps half a card's height in every state, so the unit's layout never reflows.

face.why: The half card standing out is the same light stock and dark ink as the SceneCard, never orange.

name.why: The inserted scene's name is printed medium at body size on the part of the card that stays out.

step.why: The first step of the scene is printed in caption size under its name, when there is room above the slit.

legend.why: An empty slot prints the words scene card with an arrow above the slit, flat ink on the plastic.

arrow.why: The printed arrow points into the slit in the legend's own ink, never a colour of its own.

slit.why: The slit is a narrow recess with the inverse light, the hole the card goes into.

foot.why: The room's name and the lamp sit on one printed line under the slit, on the unit's inset line.

label.why: The room or device name is printed at label size in primary ink, as the slot's own name.

announce.why: A polite hidden status says which scene went into which room, or that it was taken out.

focus-visible.why: The focused slot shows the same dark ring as every part, drawn around the bay and the slit together.

disabled.why: A slot of a unit that is offline takes no card and says so, and its printing stays readable.

data-ready=true.why: While a card is held the slit shows a ring and its legend prints at full ink, so the places it can go are seen.

data-over=true.why: The slot under a dragged card prints its ring in full ink, so the hand sees where the card will go.

data-fresh=true.why: Only a card the person just inserted slides into the slit; a card already in when the page opens stays still.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the card is in the slit at once and the ring appears without a fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the slit and the card keep outlines and the ring uses Highlight, because the recess shading fades there.

@insert.why: The inserted card travels one rise step down into the slit, fast in and slow out, and then stays still.

outline-color.why: The slit's ring fades in when a card is held through the state motion tokens, never in one frame.

color.why: The legend steps to full ink with the ring on the same timing when a card is held.
